newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin, against NATO expansion, goes to OSCE.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin, against NATO expansion, goes to OSCE.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, reiterating Russian opposition to NATO's expansion plans, left Moscow on Sunday to attend a meeting of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
Chernomyrdin told reporters that Russia would not change its stance on NATO at the Lisbon meeting, which will be attended by 54 of the OSCE's 55 member states.

"We are categorically against the expansion of NATO to the east," Interfax news agency quoted the prime minister as saying as he left Moscow. "Russia has its position and will stand by it at the OSCE meeting."
Russia has vigorously opposed NATO plans to take in some of Moscow's former East Bloc allies, but has also recognised that it can do little to halt the process.
Chernomyrdin said he accepted that Russia had no right of veto, but stressed that other states should take Moscow's opinion into account.
